stem: A critically ill child in septic shock remains unresponsive to fluids and inotropic support, what adrenal-related diagnosis should be considered?

options.text: Bilateral adrenal haemorrhage causing acute adrenal crisis
No endocrine cause needs to be considered
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency
Hyperpigmentation must be present before adrenal disease is considered
Adrenal causes are relevant only in neonates

explanation: Bilateral adrenal haemorrhage causing acute adrenal crisis should be considered in a child with refractory septic shock who does not respond to fluids and inotropic support.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Adrenal Insufficiency

optionExplanations.A: Correct because bilateral adrenal haemorrhage can cause acute adrenal crisis and should be considered in refractory septic shock.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because persistent shock despite fluids and inotropes does not exclude an endocrine cause such as adrenal crisis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because congenital adrenal hyperplasia is not the specific adrenal-related diagnosis highlighted in this scenario.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because hyperpigmentation is not required before adrenal disease should be considered.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because adrenal causes can be relevant beyond the neonatal period.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
